name: Visibility of System Status
rule: Keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable time.
location: Global Header, Contact Form, Usability Lab
implementation: Live scroll progress bar at top of viewport; active navigation link highlight synchronized with scroll spy; form submission state spinner and real-time validation badges; task timer and SUS score calculation preview.
beforeFix: Initial static form showed no indication when the submit button was clicked.
afterFix: Added animated loading state, disabled submit state with spinner, and immediate success toast with undo action.

name: Match Between System and the Real World
rule: Speak the users' language, with words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than internal jargon.
implementation: Familiar academic terms (CGPA, Coursework, Semester), standard engineering concepts (AST, REST API, VAE, Docker), natural calendar timeline metaphors, universally recognized iconography (GitHub, LinkedIn, Terminal, Book).
beforeFix: Technical skills were originally labeled with obscure internal abbreviations and arbitrary % bars.
afterFix: Replaced misleading percentages with clear competency tiers (Proficient, Working Knowledge, Exploring) and domain groupings.

name: User Control and Freedom
rule: Users often perform actions by mistake. Provide clearly marked 'emergency exits' to leave unwanted states.
location: Project Details Modal, Article Reader Modal, Command Palette
implementation: Prominent close buttons ('X') in modals; full keyboard `Escape` dismissal; click outside / backdrop dismiss; clear search button to reset filters; undo toast action on form actions.
beforeFix: Opening project details trapped users without an obvious back button or keyboard escape handler.
afterFix: Added backdrop blur click dismissal, accessible 'Esc' key event listener, and sticky top-right exit button with focus trap.

name: Consistency and Standards
rule: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing.
location: Global Design System, Typography, Button Component Hierarchy
implementation: Single unified design token system for colors, shadows, border radii, and button hierarchies (Primary accent, Secondary outline, Ghost); standardized badge anatomy across all cards.
beforeFix: Different sections utilized inconsistent button sizes and conflicting card border radii.
afterFix: Standardized all interactive elements using a centralized utility class hierarchy and tokenized spacing scale.

name: Error Prevention
rule: A careful design which prevents a problem from occurring in the first place is even better than good error messages.
location: Contact Form, SUS Evaluation Form, Search Inputs
implementation: Inline live email regex checking; disabled submit button when mandatory fields are missing; input masking; character limit counters with warning state; confirmation dialog before clearing completed evaluations.
beforeFix: Users could submit an empty or malformed contact form, triggering generic alert popups.
afterFix: Implemented proactive field validation that detects syntax errors on keystroke and disables submit until valid.

name: Recognition Rather Than Recall
rule: Minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible.
location: Sticky Header, Project Category Chips, Command Palette, Tooltips
implementation: Persistent navigation bar with visible labels; filter chips showing exact category counts; keyboard shortcut hints (`Ctrl+K`, `?`, `D`); breadcrumbs and visible metadata tags on all articles and projects.
beforeFix: Filter options required remembering exact technology names in a free-text box.
afterFix: Added visible category filter chips (AI/ML, NLP & Systems, Full Stack) alongside autocomplete search.

name: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
rule: Accelerators—unseen by novice users—may speed up the interaction for expert users.
location: Command Palette, Global Shortcuts, Quick Filter Chips
implementation: `Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K` command palette for instant navigation across all projects, blogs, and sections; `D` hotkey to toggle dark/light theme; `?` hotkey to open HCI design guide; quick copy buttons for contact info.
beforeFix: Navigation was purely mouse-driven with no keyboard accelerators for power users or evaluators.
afterFix: Implemented global hotkeys (`Ctrl+K`, `Esc`, `D`, `?`) and Tab-index navigable interface.

name: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
rule: Dialogues should not contain information that is irrelevant or rarely needed. Every extra unit of info competes.
implementation: Clean 60-30-10 color balance using slate neutral base and indigo accent; generous whitespace (24-32px margins); progressive disclosure (summaries on cards, deep architecture inside modal dialogs).
beforeFix: Project cards were overcrowded with full paragraphs of text, raw URLs, and cluttered metrics.
afterFix: Streamlined cards to high-level subtitle + key metrics + 3 tech tags; moved architecture deep-dive into modal dialog.

name: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
rule: Error messages should be expressed in plain language, precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.
location: Contact Form Inline Errors, Search Zero State
implementation: Clear, contextual error messages with actionable suggestions ('Please enter a valid email address with an @ symbol and domain'); zero-state fallback with a one-click 'Clear Filters' button when no projects match.
beforeFix: Searching for an unmatched keyword resulted in a blank screen with no guidance.
afterFix: Added friendly empty-state illustration with text: 'No projects match your filter. Click here to reset all filters'.

name: Help and Documentation
rule: Even though it is better if the system can be used without documentation, it may be necessary to provide help.
location: HCI Guide Modal, Feature Tooltips, Evaluation Instructions
implementation: Accessible 'HCI Principles & Navigation Guide' modal accessible via floating badge or `?` hotkey; descriptive tooltips explaining technical metrics (e.g. 'AST', 'VAE', 'HDBSCAN', 'SUS score formula').
beforeFix: Evaluators had to guess which HCI heuristics were implemented in which components.
afterFix: Integrated on-demand interactive HCI inspector highlighting real-time design decisions and heuristic mappings.
